200.description:
One entity of the consolidated list by its own identifier: `eu:<logicalId>` (the source_record_id), a bare logicalId, or the EU reference number (EU.n.n). Returns the full record (names in every language and script with their amendment reference, identifiers, addresses with contact details, nationalities, birth dates and places kept as partial or approximate as the file states them, programme, measures, legal basis with EUR-Lex links, designation date or its fallback, UN reference, designation details, remarks) plus the publication it was read from. There is no per-entity endpoint upstream: the call reads the feed and the current XML 1.1 file and stops at the matching entity. Fails with not_found when no entity in the current file carries the identifier.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `addresses` | object[] |  |
| `birth_dates` | object[] | One entry per birthdate element; partial and approximate dates are kept as given (date null with only a year, year ranges, circa). |
| `birth_places` | object[] | Place parts of the birthdate elements that carry any (same logical_id as the birth date). |
| `designation_details` | string |  |
| `entity_type` | string | subjectType@code mapped: person -> person, enterprise -> organization. The file has no vessel or aircraft subject type; vessels appear as organizations with an `imo` identifier. |
| `eu_reference_number` | string | sanctionEntity@euReferenceNumber (EU.n.n); present on every entity of the 1.1 file. |
| `identifiers` | object[] |  |
| `legal_basis` | object[] |  |
| `listed_on` | string | sanctionEntity@designationDate; when the file omits it, the earliest regulationSummary publicationDate under the entity (see listed_on_source). |
| `listed_on_source` | string |  |
| `logical_id` | number | sanctionEntity@logicalId, the stable integer id the file is sorted by. |
| `measures` | string[] | Always asset_freeze: the Financial Sanctions Files cover the asset-freeze measure only. Travel bans are not in this source even when a remark mentions one. |
| `names` | object[] |  |
| `nationalities` | object[] |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `primary_name` | string | wholeName of the nameAlias with the lowest logicalId (the file's name order changes between publications). |
| `programs` | string[] | regulation@programme codes (UKR, IRN, SYR, ...); one per entity in the current file. |
| `publication` | object | The publication the record was read from (record_count omitted: the walk stops at the match). |
| `publication_id` | string | SHA-1 checksum of the file, as posted by the publisher in the RSS guid and verified against the downloaded bytes. |
| `remarks` | string[] | Free-text remarks on this element, as published (may be empty). |
| `retrieved_at` | string | UTC time of the download, ISO 8601. |
| `source_record_id` | string | Namespaced id: `eu:` + sanctionEntity@logicalId. |
| `source_url` | string | The XML 1.1 file resource the record was read from (URL without the public access query parameter printed in the feed; there is no per-entity page). |
| `subject_type` | object |  |
| `un_reference` | string | sanctionEntity@unitedNationId when UN-listed (e.g. LYi.006). |

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous page. Opaque; pinned to the publication the first page came from.

entity_type.description:
Keep only persons (subjectType person) or organizations (subjectType enterprise).

Provider reference: allowed values ["person", "organization"].

page_size.description:
Entities per page (default 200). A record is 1 to 60 KB of JSON; 500 entities of the list are roughly 2.5 MB.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 500; default 200.

programme.description: Regulation programme code as written in the file (UKR, IRN, SYR, BLR, TAQA, PRK, ...). Case-insensitive. An unknown code fails with invalid_input listing the codes in the file.

200.description:
One page of the full consolidated list (XML 1.1), in file order (ascending logicalId), optionally filtered by programme code (UKR, IRN, SYR, ... 34 codes in the current file) and entity type (person, organization). The cursor is pinned to the publication (the file's SHA-1): every page re-reads the feed and the file, and when the publication has moved on the call fails with invalid_input, issue code `publication_changed`, instead of mixing two versions; restart without a cursor. Each record carries source_record_id (eu:<logicalId>), entity_type, primary_name, names (all languages and scripts), identifiers, addresses, nationalities, birth_dates (partial and approximate kept as given), birth_places, programs, measures (always asset_freeze), legal_basis, listed_on (designationDate, or the earliest amendment date when the file omits it), un_reference, remarks, and the provenance fields source_url, publication_id, retrieved_at. `total` counts the entities matching the filter in the whole file; `publication.record_count` is the file's entity count. Every page costs one feed request and one gzip-compressed download of the 25 MB file (about 2.5 MB on the wire), so prefer large pages (up to 500).

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `records` as the primary payload key.

limit.description:
Maximum hits returned (default 25).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 25.

programme.description: Restrict to one programme code (UKR, IRN, ...).

q.description: Name or name fragment; terms are matched as substrings, all must match the same name.

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
Name search over the current consolidated list: every whitespace-separated term of `q` must occur (case-insensitive substring) in one of an entity's names, in any language or script (nameAlias wholeName). Optional programme and entity_type filters. Returns compact hits in file order (source_record_id, EU reference number, entity type, primary name, the names that matched, programmes, listing date, UN reference); records_get has the full record. `total` counts every matching entity; when it exceeds `limit` the result is marked partial. An empty result is a legitimate answer (no name contains the terms), not an error. A match or an absence is not a compliance determination.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `results` as the primary payload key.

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
Cheap version check from the RSS feed (one 4 KB request, no file download): the current XML 1.1 publication's id (the publisher's SHA-1 checksum of the file, from the feed's guid), publication date, file resource URL (without the public access query parameter the feed prints; see file_url), size in bytes and content hash, plus the same for every published file (PDF 1.0, CSV 1.0, CSV 1.1, XML 1.1, XML 1.0). The record count is not returned here because it needs the 25 MB file; records_list returns it. Use the publication_id to decide whether a held snapshot is stale.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content_hash` | object |  |
| `file_id` | string | The file identifier in the URL path (xmlFullSanctionsList_1_1). |
| `file_url` | string | URL of the XML 1.1 file resource (the feed's link without its query string). The server requires the public access query parameter the publisher prints in clear in the feed's <link>/<enclosure>; the program reads it from the feed at runtime. Outputs omit it so that recorded examples carry no credential-looking strings. |
| `files` | object[] | Every item of the feed, in feed order. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `publication_id` | string | SHA-1 of the XML 1.1 file as posted by the publisher (RSS guid checksum). Changes with every publication. |
| `published_at` | string | RSS pubDate of the XML 1.1 item, ISO 8601 UTC. |
| `retrieved_at` | string |  |
| `size_bytes` | number | RSS enclosure length of the XML 1.1 file. |
| `source_url` | string |  |
